chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā and al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān together, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about madhy, and he said: Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام was a man who experienced much madhy, so he felt shy to ask the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم because of the position of Fāṭimah عليها السلام. So he instructed al-Miqdād to ask him while he was sitting, and he asked him. Then the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to him: It is not anything.

key_terms.الْمَذْيِ: pre-seminal fluid being asked about in the legal ruling
key_terms.الْمِقْدَادَ: the companion instructed to ask on behalf of ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ: the Messenger of Allah, the one being asked for the ruling
key_terms.فَاطِمَةَ عَلَيْهَا السَّلَامُ: Fāṭimah عليها السلام, mentioned as the reason for ʿAlī's modesty
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِشَيْءٍ: it is not anything; the Prophet's concise legal response
key_terms.مَذَّاءً: one who frequently experiences discharge of madhy

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on madhy in Shia hadith, and what did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم say about it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of madhy and reports that Amir al-Mu'minin ʿAlī عليه السلام, out of modesty due to Fāṭimah عليها السلام, did not ask the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم directly. The Prophet's reply, "It is not anything," indicates that madhy is not treated here as carrying the legal consequence being asked about.
